body.statement:
Let \((X_1,\Sigma_1,\mu_1)\) and \((X_2,\Sigma_2,\mu_2)\) be \(\sigma\)-finite measure spaces.  If \(f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,\infty]\) is measurable, then
\[
 \int_{X_1\times X_2} f\,d(\mu_1\otimes\mu_2)
 =\int_{X_1}\!\left(\int_{X_2}f(x_1,x_2)\,d\mu_2(x_2)\right)d\mu_1(x_1)
 =\int_{X_2}\!\left(\int_{X_1}f(x_1,x_2)\,d\mu_1(x_1)\right)d\mu_2(x_2).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(f\in\mathcal M_+(X_1\times X_2,\Sigma_1\otimes\Sigma_2)\). Then, we have \(\int_{X_1\times X_2}f\,d(\mu_1\otimes\mu_2)=\int_{X_1}(\int_{X_2}f_{x_1}\,d\mu_2)\,d\mu_1=\int_{X_2}(\int_{X_1}f^{x_2}\,d\mu_1)\,d\mu_2\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the theorem displayed in the Introduction of Boldo, Clément, Martin, Mayero, and Mouhcine, arXiv:2202.05040.

body.justification: This is the nonnegative product-integration theorem used to exchange expectation and Lebesgue integration in the common-mass length argument.
body.gap: None; only the stated nonnegative, measurable, \(\sigma\)-finite case is used.
body.consumer: The masked-continuum lemma applies the theorem to an interval-membership indicator under one extended probability law and finite Lebesgue measure.
